text:
eric: FYI I pushed a draft PRD + runtime RFC for the adaptive kernel routing + prefix cache TTL adjustments. link: https://rwd.in/notes/adaptive-routing-draft. Need triage for Q3 roadmap planning — main asks: define launch criteria, acceptance tests, edge cases, and a canary/rollback plan. Please skim and drop comments here.

leah: reading it now. quick q: are we gating on p95 or p99 for the launch SLO? also do we care about long-context (>64k) models in this rollout or keep them out?

maria: my suggested seeds for acceptance criteria (we can iterate):
```
- p95 latency <= 120ms for 2k context base models
- p95 latency <= 250ms for >16k context models (if included)
- end-to-end quality regression <= 2% on the eval suite (LLM-coherence tests)
- unit token cost delta <= +5% vs current baseline
- no server crashes / kernel mismatch exceptions in 48h canary
```
Canary: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor p95/p99, error_rate and correctness probes. rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or quality regression > 2.5%.

dan: one edge case we should call out: prefix cache thrash when customers use tons of unique prefixes (e.g., multi-tenant chat with per-user prefixes). we should add an adaptive TTL and a hard eviction policy. proposal: default TTL=60s, increase to max 600s for prefixes with freq>100 reqs/min in last 10m.

alex: kernel selection note: it must be deterministic given (model_id, seq_len, quant_mode). if we change heuristic we need a compatibility table so older clients don't break. fallback: route to generic-compat kernel when no match. Also add a guard so a kernel fallback never increases memory by >10% otherwise it could OOM.

sophia: testing matrix ideas: small models (7B), medium (34B), large (70B), quantized and non-quantized variants, short/long contexts, and a synthetic workload that forces prefix churn. include perf profiles and offline eval results in the RFC.

eric: good points. let's lock a minimal launch scope to reduce blast radius:
- scope v1: kernel routing + adaptive prefix TTL for hosted API only, base models up to 34B, quantized variants supported. exclude >64k contexts and Dedicated private clusters for the first canary.
- scope v2: expand to long-context and Dedicated after we hit canary gates.

maria: can we add concrete rollout gates in the PRD? e.g.,
```
Rollout gates:
1) Perf gate: p95 <= baseline + 10ms on canary (all model groups)
2) Stability: system error_rate < 0.2% over 48h
3) Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 98%
4) Cost: token unit-cost increase <= 7%
```
If any gate fails, auto-rollback and page oncall.

dan: add a gate for cache thrash telemetry: if prefix cache eviction rate > X (we should pick a number), or cache hitrate drops > 15% vs baseline, pause rollout.

alex: ops/infra ask: include a debug flag to force use of new routing per-request (for repro) and a metric that tags which kernel was chosen in traces. don't forget to add the new kernel name to the kernel catalog mapping.

eric: agreed. action items:
- maria to author acceptance criteria section in PRD and add the gate numbers (owner: maria)
- dan to propose adaptive TTL algorithm and telemetry thresholds (owner: dan)
- alex to add kernel compatibility table + fallback spec (owner: alex)
- leah to draft canary runbook and alert thresholds (owner: leah)
- sophia to produce testing matrix + synthetic workload harness (owner: sophia)
- eric to update roadmap item and add to Q3 planning doc

leah: I'll also add a short checklist for launch readiness: docs, console labels, cost signals, rollout toggles, and customer comms templates (in case we need to notify large customers).

deploy-bot: scheduled canary window suggested: 1963460000 (UTC) - please confirm owners and blockers.

maria: owners confirmed. blocker: we need automated correctness probes in CI for kernel fallbacks — I'll open a small PR to add that today.

eric: perfect. let's reconvene Friday sync with PRD link and first drafts attached. :thumbsup:

leah: quick nit — include a short paragraph under 'Edge cases' about GDPR-sensitive prompt prefixes (do not cache if a prefix is flagged sensitive). we should default to not caching those.

alex: good call. add a config knob to opt-in to caching for sensitive tenants (org-level flag).

eric: added to action list. thanks all.

sophia: putting a note in the RFC to capture expected perf-cost tradeoff table so PM/product can make prioritization decisions.

eric: closing loop here — I'll push an updated RFC with the points above by EOD and tag reviewers. if anyone has last-minute asks, drop them here.
